title: Aether Traversal
summary: Momentum-based traversal sandbox where motion is the core reward.
description: A third-person traversal prototype exploring flow-state movement. Players chain grapples, wall-runs and air-dashes across a floating archipelago, where speed unlocks routes and rewards mastery.

caseStudy.problem: Traversal in open sandboxes often feels like a chore between objectives instead of the fun itself.
caseStudy.solution: Designed a momentum economy: every input either preserves or converts speed, so skilled routing is intrinsically rewarding without extrinsic collectibles.
challenges: Tuning a stable momentum curve that felt fast but controllable at 60 FPS
Preventing camera nausea during high-speed chained maneuvers
Authoring readable level geometry that telegraphs optimal lines
learnings: Kinesthetic feedback (FOV kick, audio pitch, trails) sells speed more than raw velocity
Grey-box iteration speed matters more than fidelity for movement tuning

gameDesign.coreLoop: Observe route -> build momentum -> chain traversal -> reach vista -> spot next route
gameDesign.playerMotivation: Mastery and self-expression through optimized movement lines
gameDesign.riskReward: Faster lines pass over lethal gaps; failure resets momentum, not progress
gameDesign.progression: New verbs (dash, grapple, glide) layer combinatorially rather than linearly
gameDesign.replayability: Ghost races and time trials on hand-authored and remixable tracks
gameDesign.technicalChallenges: Deterministic movement for ghost replays across framerates

title: Signal Forge
summary: A crafting economy driven by emergent supply-and-demand simulation.
description: Systems design for a survival-crafting title. Recipes, resources and NPC factions form a closed economy where scarcity emerges from player behavior rather than scripted spawns.

caseStudy.problem: Static loot tables made the mid-game economy collapse into a single dominant strategy.
caseStudy.solution: Modeled a feedback-driven economy in Machinations, then ported tuned curves into a data-driven ScriptableObject pipeline for rapid balancing.
challenges: Avoiding runaway inflation loops in the faction trade AI
Exposing enough economic signals for players to read scarcity
Keeping simulation cost under 1ms/frame for low-end targets
learnings: Second-order effects need telemetry dashboards, not intuition
Designers iterate 10x faster when balance lives in data, not code

gameDesign.coreLoop: Gather -> refine -> trade -> invest -> unlock deeper tiers
gameDesign.riskReward: Specializing yields profit but exposes players to demand shocks
gameDesign.progression: Tech tree gates access to higher-volatility, higher-margin goods
gameDesign.replayability: Procedural faction demands reshape the optimal build each run
gameDesign.technicalChallenges: Deterministic economy sim with rollback for multiplayer

title: Lumen Weave
summary: Volumetric, hand-painted light shafts running fully in real time.
description: A collection of stylized lighting shaders: screen-space god rays, iridescent surfaces and animated caustics designed to feel painterly while staying performant on mid-tier GPUs.

caseStudy.problem: Physically based volumetrics were too expensive and too realistic for the target art direction.
caseStudy.solution: Authored a layered noise-driven light-shaft shader with artist-facing controls, decoupling look from cost via LOD-aware sample counts.
challenges: Temporal stability of noise under camera motion
Keeping the effect under 1.2ms at 1440p
Exposing intuitive knobs for non-technical artists
learnings: Blue-noise dithering fixes banding cheaper than more samples
Artist trust grows when parameters map to visual intent, not math

title: Warden AI
summary: Readable stealth AI built on a transparent perception model.
description: Technical design of a stealth encounter system: a utility-driven guard AI whose senses, alertness and search behavior are fully legible to players through diegetic feedback.

caseStudy.problem: Players felt stealth failures were unfair because guard perception was a black box.
caseStudy.solution: Built a layered perception model (sight cones, hearing falloff, last-known-position) with UI and audio tells for every state transition.
challenges: Balancing challenge with total predictability
Coordinating multi-guard search without gamey teleporting
Debugging non-deterministic AI across encounter replays
learnings: Telegraphing state changes turns frustration into tactical planning
EQS made search patterns feel intelligent without bespoke scripting

gameDesign.coreLoop: Observe patrol -> plan route -> act -> react to alert -> reposition
gameDesign.playerMotivation: Tactical mastery and the power fantasy of the ghost
gameDesign.riskReward: Aggressive routes save time but raise the alert ceiling
gameDesign.progression: Tools (distractions, takedowns) expand the tactical vocabulary
gameDesign.replayability: Systemic guards create emergent, non-scripted encounters
gameDesign.technicalChallenges: Deterministic perception for reliable QA reproduction

title: Forge Runes
summary: A procedural rune-inscription tool for artists, built as an editor plugin.
description: Technical art tooling that lets artists paint glowing runes onto any mesh with animated emissive flow, packaged as a reusable Unreal editor utility.

caseStudy.problem: Hand-placing animated runes per asset took artists days and looked inconsistent.
caseStudy.solution: Built a spline-and-mask driven tool that bakes rune flow maps and auto-configures a shared material, cutting authoring time to minutes.
challenges: UV-independent placement across arbitrary topology
Keeping baked textures within memory budget
Designing a UX artists could learn in one session
learnings: Great tools disappear into the artist's workflow
A tight feedback loop in-editor beats an external baking step

title: Rift Protocol
summary: Networked ability system for a 3v3 arena brawler vertical slice.
description: A gameplay ability system (GAS) implementation for a competitive arena game: server-authoritative abilities, client prediction and rollback-friendly cooldowns.

caseStudy.problem: Ability responsiveness suffered on high-latency connections, breaking the competitive feel.
caseStudy.solution: Implemented client-side prediction with server reconciliation for the ability pipeline, keeping inputs snappy while preserving authority.
challenges: Reconciling mispredicted ability activations gracefully
Keeping cooldown state consistent under packet loss
Profiling replication bandwidth within budget
learnings: Prediction is a UX feature, not just a netcode detail

gameDesign.coreLoop: Engage -> combo abilities -> manage cooldowns -> reposition -> secure objective
gameDesign.riskReward: Committing an ultimate wins fights but leaves a long vulnerability window
gameDesign.progression: Ranked ladder and mastery unlocks per character
gameDesign.replayability: Counterplay depth from a compact but combinatorial kit
gameDesign.technicalChallenges: Lag compensation and rollback-safe ability timing

title: Oracle Forge
summary: An AI-assisted level-blockout copilot for rapid greyboxing.
description: An in-editor AI tool that turns natural-language design intent into parametric blockout layouts, giving designers a fast starting point they can refine by hand.

caseStudy.problem: Blockout iteration stalled early because a blank level is intimidating and slow to fill.
caseStudy.solution: Built a copilot that proposes graph-based layouts from prompts, snapping to design metrics (sightlines, pacing beats) as editable modules.
challenges: Constraining generative output to shippable design grammar
Making suggestions editable rather than throwaway
Keeping designers in control and the AI advisory
learnings: AI tools win by accelerating the first draft, not replacing judgment
Design constraints as guardrails make generation trustworthy

title: Tempo Strike
summary: Rhythm-melee prototype where combat lives on the beat.
description: A gameplay prototype fusing character-action combat with rhythm timing. Attacks land harder on-beat, turning encounters into improvised musical performances.

caseStudy.problem: Rhythm games punish mistakes harshly; action players resented losing agency to a metronome.
caseStudy.solution: Made the beat a bonus layer, not a gate: off-beat play still works, on-beat play amplifies. Forgiveness windows scale with difficulty.
challenges: Syncing input, audio and animation within one frame of tolerance
Communicating the beat without a distracting HUD
Balancing accessibility with skill expression
learnings: Game feel is 90% timing windows and audio-visual confirmation
Optional depth respects both casual and expert players

gameDesign.coreLoop: Read enemy tell -> strike on beat -> chain combo -> spend meter -> reset tempo
gameDesign.playerMotivation: Flow, rhythm mastery and stylish expression
gameDesign.riskReward: On-beat parries are high-risk, high-style, high-reward
gameDesign.progression: New rhythmic verbs and tracks raise the skill ceiling
gameDesign.replayability: Score-attack encounters and remixable enemy charts
